content: Yes, it is true. In Switzerland, every person who is at least 18 years old and holds Swiss citizenship is eligible to vote. However, to actually exercise this right, Swiss citizens must first register with the local municipality (Gemeinde) at their place of residence. Registration is required to receive voting materials and to be included on the electoral roll. The federal government does not handle voter registration; this is the responsibility of the municipalities. Once registered, voters can participate in federal, cantonal, and municipal votes and elections.
